headline: Recursive launches Flint, a laptop coding model it says was largely built by AI
snapshot: Startup Recursive has released Flint, a free, laptop-sized coding model built largely by its own AI research system, as an early test of AI that improves itself. The competitive question is whether this changes the model race, enterprise integrations or customer lock-in as major AI providers battle for durable platform advantage.

editor_signals.headline: Anthropic pitches AI safety bill that may block a model if 50+ people could be killed
editor_signals.snapshot: The proposed policy seems to offer protections against AI running amok but actually forbids federal agencies from blocking a model's release without the permission of a judge. The story matters because AI is moving deeper into legal and regulatory territory, where product speed, data rights, safety obligations and public accountability can affect adoption.
